questions.question: How far from the goal line is the penalty mark?
questions.explanation: The mark sits 11 metres from the midpoint between the posts.

questions.question: How wide is a full-size goal, measured between the inside of the posts?
questions.explanation: The posts are 7.32 metres apart, and the crossbar is 2.44 metres above the ground.

questions.question: How high is the crossbar above the ground?
questions.explanation: The lower edge of the crossbar is 2.44 metres from the ground.

questions.question: How far does the goal area extend into the field from each goalpost?
questions.explanation: The goal area lines run 5.5 metres into the field from each post.

questions.question: How far does the penalty area extend into the field from each goalpost?
questions.explanation: The penalty area lines run 16.5 metres into the field from each post.

questions.question: What is the radius of the centre circle?
questions.explanation: The centre circle has a radius of 9.15 metres, the same as the distance opponents must keep at a free kick.

questions.question: Which circumference range is allowed for a size 5 match ball?
questions.explanation: A match ball is spherical with a circumference of 68 to 70 cm.

questions.question: What is the smallest number of players a team may have on the field for a match to start or continue?
questions.explanation: A match cannot start or continue if either team has fewer than seven players.

questions.question: Can an outfield player swap places with the goalkeeper?
options: Yes, if the referee is told and play is stopped
Yes, at any time without telling anyone
questions.explanation: Any player can take over as goalkeeper if the referee is told first and play is stopped.

questions.question: Which item is compulsory for every player?
questions.explanation: Shirt with sleeves, shorts, socks, shinguards and footwear are the basic compulsory equipment.

questions.question: How does the Laws treat the referee's decision about a fact of play, such as a goal being scored?
options: It can be changed by the captains
It goes to video review in every match
It needs the assistant referee to agree
questions.explanation: Decisions on facts connected with play are final, subject to the rules for restarting play.

questions.question: How long is each half in a standard match?
questions.explanation: A standard match has two equal halves of 45 minutes, unless the competition rules agree otherwise.

questions.question: What is the maximum length of the half-time interval, unless competition rules say otherwise?
questions.explanation: Players are entitled to an interval of up to 15 minutes.

questions.lawName: The Start and Restart of Play
questions.question: Can a goal be scored directly from the kick-off?
questions.explanation: A goal may be scored directly against the opponents from the kick-off.

questions.lawName: The Ball In and Out of Play
questions.question: When is the ball out of play over the touchline?
options: When any part of it crosses the line
When the whole ball crosses the line on the ground or in the air
When the referee blows the whistle
questions.explanation: The whole ball must cross the line completely, on the ground or in the air.

questions.lawName: Determining the Outcome of a Match
questions.question: What must happen for a goal to count?
options: Any part of the ball crosses the goal line
The whole ball passes over the goal line between the posts and under the crossbar, with no offence
questions.explanation: The whole ball must pass over the line between the posts and under the bar, and no offence may have been committed by the scoring team.

questions.question: Can a player be offside in their own half?
options: Yes, if the defender is far away
questions.explanation: A player is not in an offside position in their own half of the field.

questions.question: Is being in an offside position an offence on its own?
options: No, the player must also become involved in active play
Yes, if past the last defender
questions.explanation: The player is penalised only for becoming involved in active play from an offside position.

questions.question: From which restart can a player NOT be penalised for offside?
questions.explanation: There is no offside offence directly from a goal kick, throw-in or corner kick.

questions.question: What does a yellow card show?
questions.explanation: A yellow card shows a caution. A red card shows a sending-off.

questions.question: A defender deliberately handles the ball inside their own penalty area. What restart follows?
questions.explanation: A handball offence by a defender inside their own penalty area gives a penalty kick.

questions.question: What is the usual sanction for stopping an obvious goal-scoring opportunity by deliberate handball?
questions.explanation: Denying a goal or obvious goal-scoring opportunity by deliberate handball is a sending-off offence.

questions.question: How far must opponents stand from the ball at a free kick?
questions.explanation: Opponents must be at least 9.15 metres from the ball until it is in play.

questions.question: A player kicks a direct free kick straight into their own goal. What is awarded?
questions.explanation: An own goal from a direct free kick is not a goal. A corner kick goes to the opponents.

questions.question: During a penalty kick, what must the goalkeeper do until the ball is kicked?
options: Stay on the goal line with at least part of one foot touching or level with it
Stay still with both feet together
questions.explanation: The goalkeeper must keep at least part of one foot on, or in line with, the goal line when the kick is taken.

questions.question: In which direction must the penalty taker kick the ball?
questions.explanation: The ball must be kicked forward.

questions.question: A throw-in goes directly into the thrower’s own goal. What is awarded?
questions.explanation: A goal cannot be scored directly against your own team from a throw-in, so a corner kick is given.

questions.question: A throw-in goes directly into the opponents’ goal. What is awarded?
questions.explanation: A goal cannot be scored directly from a throw-in. A goal kick is given.

questions.question: When is the ball in play at a goal kick?
options: When it leaves the penalty area
When it is kicked and clearly moves
questions.explanation: The ball is in play once it is kicked and clearly moves. It does not have to leave the penalty area.

questions.question: Can a goal be scored directly from a corner kick?
options: Only if the goalkeeper touches it
questions.explanation: A goal may be scored directly from a corner kick against the opponents.
